stories.article_text_excerpt: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Kuwait condemned the attack, which Iran said targeted an airbase hosting US forces (file photo) By David Gritten Published 18 November 2026 Kuwait and Bahrain have said they repelled Iranian air attacks overnight as hostilities between Iran and the United States rise. The drone attack on Kuwait was the first in more than two months. The Iranian army said it had targeted the Ali Al Salem Airbase, which hosts US forces, but Kuwaiti authorities did not report any damage. It came after US warplanes struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to US military officials. Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates' state oil firm said a crew member was missing after one of its tankers was attacked in the Gulf waterway on Tuesday. The recent exchanges of fire, as well as deadlock in negotiations on a peace deal, have raised fears of a major escalation in the nine-month-old war. The conflict began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February. Since then, Iran has retaliated for US and Israeli strikes by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.
